summary.text: Ron Watson is a Democratic Maryland state senator from District 23 who has held the seat since August 2021 and is seeking re-election in the November 3, 2026 general election.
A U.S. Army Reserve veteran with a Ph.D. in systems science, he works in business management and IT consulting.

paragraphs.text: Ron Watson was born in Washington, D.C., on April 30, 1966, and graduated from Central Senior High School in 1984.

He earned a B.S. in electrical engineering from Morgan State University in 1991, a Ph.D. in systems science from Binghamton University in 1999, and an M.B.A. from George Washington University in 2002.
Watson served in the U.S. Army Reserves from 1989 to 2006, reaching the rank of major.

His career included program-management roles at Lockheed Martin Mission Systems, IBM Global Services and MCR, and since 2004 he has been president and senior program manager of Watson Management Corporation.
Watson was elected to the Maryland House of Delegates in District 23B, serving from 2019 to 2021.
Gov. Larry Hogan, a Republican, appointed him to the state Senate in August 2021 to fill the vacancy created when Douglas Peters resigned.
Watson serves on the Education, Energy, and the Environment Committee, according to the General Assembly website.
